title: Ulysses
description: A single day in Dublin, 16 June 1904, follows Leopold Bloom, Stephen Dedalus and Molly Bloom. Its experimental style made it a landmark of modernist fiction.
places: The whole novel unfolds across Dublin.
Bloom buys lemon soap here in the Lotus Eaters episode.
The opening scene takes place on the roof of this tower.
Sylvia Beach's original shop published the first edition.

title: Dubliners
description: Fifteen linked short stories portray ordinary lives in early twentieth-century Dublin, from childhood through public life.
places: Every story is set in or around Dublin.
Exhibitions and tours on Joyce and his Dublin.

title: The Great Gatsby
description: Nick Carraway watches his wealthy neighbour Jay Gatsby chase a lost love in Jazz Age New York.
places: The hotel suite confrontation is the novel's turning point.
Fitzgerald lived here and West Egg is commonly read as modelled on it.

title: Pride and Prejudice
description: Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy overcome pride and misjudgement in Regency England.
places: Austen revised the novel for publication while living here.

title: Persuasion
description: Anne Elliot gets a second chance at love eight years after being persuaded to refuse Captain Wentworth.
places: The later chapters are set in Bath.
Louisa Musgrove's fall happens on the Cobb.
Austen wrote the novel while living at Chawton.

title: Les Misérables
description: Jean Valjean's search for redemption unfolds against poverty, justice and revolution in nineteenth-century France.
places: Large parts of the story take place in Paris.
Hugo lived here when he began work on the book.

title: A Study in Scarlet
description: The first story to introduce Sherlock Holmes and Dr Watson, who investigate a murder in London.
places: The fictional address 221B Baker Street is introduced here.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
description: Holmes and Watson investigate a family curse involving a spectral hound on a lonely moor.
places: The story is set on Dartmoor in Devon.
Holmes's Baker Street rooms frame the case.

title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
description: An orphaned boy learns he is a wizard and starts school at Hogwarts.
places: Harry catches the Hogwarts Express from Platform 9¾.

title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
description: Seven generations of the Buendía family live and fall in the fictional town of Macondo.
places: The author's birthplace is widely linked to Macondo.

title: The Shadow of the Wind
description: A boy discovers a forgotten book in a hidden library and searches for its vanished author.
places: The story follows Barcelona after the Civil War.

title: Norwegian Wood
description: Toru Watanabe looks back on love, loss and friendship as a student in the late 1960s.
places: Most of the story takes place in Tokyo.

title: The Name of the Rose
description: A Franciscan friar investigates murders in a medieval Italian abbey.
places: Often cited as one inspiration for the fictional abbey.

title: Don Quixote
description: A gentleman who reads too many chivalric romances sets out to revive knight-errantry with his squire Sancho Panza.
places: Local tradition links these windmills to the giants Quixote fights.

title: A Moveable Feast
description: Hemingway's memoir recalls his early years as a writer in 1920s Paris.
places: The memoir recalls Hemingway's years in Paris.
Hemingway describes borrowing books from Sylvia Beach's shop.
Described as a place where he wrote.

title: The Sun Also Rises
description: A group of American and British expatriates travel from Paris to the fiesta at Pamplona.
places: The fiesta of San Fermín is the novel's centrepiece.
Hemingway frequented the café, but the novel does not name it.

title: Anne of Green Gables
description: An imaginative orphan girl changes the lives of the Cuthberts in rural Prince Edward Island.
places: The farm and its landscape inspired the book's setting.

title: Wuthering Heights
description: A turbulent love between Heathcliff and Catherine Earnshaw plays out on the Yorkshire moors.
places: Emily wrote the novel while living at the parsonage.

title: Crime and Punishment
description: A destitute student commits a murder and wrestles with guilt in Saint Petersburg.
places: Raskolnikov's story is set in real districts of the city.
Dostoevsky's last home, though he wrote another novel there.

title: The Master and Margarita
description: The devil visits Soviet Moscow while a writer's novel about Pontius Pilate takes shape.

title: Little Women
description: Four sisters grow up in Massachusetts during and after the American Civil War.
places: Alcott wrote the novel here and drew on the house.

title: Walden
description: Thoreau reflects on simple living and nature during two years in a cabin at Walden Pond.
places: The book describes life on the shore of the pond.

title: On the Road
description: Sal Paradise and Dean Moriarty crisscross the United States in a restless search for experience.
places: Linked through the Beat circle, not through a scene in the novel.
